_source: build-doc §9.7 asset manifest · §9.1 pipeline · §9.2 locked generation parameters · §9.3 post-process chain · §8.4 style lock. Rows carry id, class, subject string, view, seed, target size and status exactly as §9.7 specifies.
_derivation: rows[] IS DERIVED — never hand-edited. `npx tsx tools/comfy/comfy-batch.ts rebuild` regenerates every row from data/species.json, data/gyms.json, data/nodes/*.json, core/types.ts PROP_KINDS and the authored blocks below, and tests/unit/manifest.test.ts fails if the committed rows differ from a fresh derivation. That is the G2 gate: a species, node or gym leader cannot exist in the manifest without existing in data/, and cannot exist in data/ without appearing here.
_authoredBlocks: Everything prefixed `_` below is AUTHORED CONTENT, transcribed from docs/content-bible.md with a per-entry source. It lives here rather than in data/ because data/ is Lane A's and carries no art copy; it is the art lane's transcription of the bible, subject to G2 exactly as data/ is.
_seedRule: seed = pin ?? hashSeed(version, id) using core/rng.ts's FNV-1a (§8.1's own hash — no second generator, G11). A row's seed is therefore a pure function of its id and its version, which is what makes G5 mechanical: regenerating an asset re-derives the SAME seed, and the only way to get a different one is to bump `version`, which is the manifest-entry versioning §8.4 licenses. `recordedSeed` freezes the seed actually used the first time a row produced a file; the runner refuses to submit a different seed for that row unless the version moved (SeedReuseError).

_credits._source: build-doc §9.1 / G13 — a projected credit estimate and an explicit --confirm before any batch ≥ 20 rows.
_credits._finding: Comfy Cloud exposes NO credit-balance endpoint (/api/customers/credit, /api/credit, /api/user/credit all 404), so the estimate cannot be read from the API. It is a measured per-image figure or it is nothing.
_credits.measuredFrom: Dashboard delta, 2026-08-26. cloud.comfy.org account menu read 4,147 before the first trial and 4,127 after 18 generations at 1024x1024 — 20 credits / 18 images = 1.11, recorded as 1.12 so the projection rounds against us. Read from the UI because Comfy Cloud exposes no credit endpoint (see _finding). A later reading over a mixed batch that included 256x256 health probes came out near 0.53 per image, so 1.12 is the 1024x1024 figure and small probes cost materially less.
_credits.note: null means UNCALIBRATED. The runner still refuses a ≥20-row batch without --confirm; it prints the row count and states plainly that the per-image cost has never been measured, rather than inventing a number. Supply --credits-per-image=N (read off the dashboard before/after a known batch) and the runner records it here.
_credits._dryRunNote: `--credits-per-image=N` prints the calibrated projection but does not persist on a --dry-run, so this pair was written directly. The number is the measurement above, not an estimate — G13 forbids inventing one.

_deviations.finding: 154 battle sprites is arithmetically impossible against the shipped roster. data/species.json holds 27 lines of which 3 are Ancients; 24 aging lines × 3 age forms + 3 Ancients × 1 form = 75 forms. It was 75 forms × front/back = 150 rows until the BACK VIEW WAS CUT: Hank ruled "we're not going to have the backs of any of the creatures. Both creatures are going to be facing forward in battle", so a form has ONE sprite and the count is 75.
_deviations.action: The manifest derives 75 creature-battle rows from data/species.json, one FRONT sprite per form. The front/back loop is gone from deriveRows: it iterates classes["creature-battle"].views, which now holds only "front", so a back row cannot be re-derived by a rebuild. §9.7's 154 is the number an art reviewer counts against, so the gap is stated here rather than discovered mid-review. game/ui/BattleHud.ts::Facing is the runtime half of the same ruling.

_deviations.finding: rembg is a Python/ONNX salient-object segmenter; it is not installed, it is not deterministic across versions, and it is not idempotent — a second pass re-mattes an already-matted sprite.
_deviations.action: Background removal is a border flood fill against the flat generated background key. Every prompt ends in `plain white background` (the §9.2 skeleton, verbatim), so the background is a known flat key, not an unknown photograph. The fill is exact, deterministic and idempotent, which is what §9.3's own 'every step idempotent' clause requires and what §10.4's idempotency test measures. If a class ever generates on a non-flat background, that class needs a real matte and this note is where to start.

_deviations.finding: §9.3's chain starts at 'nearest-neighbour downscale to target'. The raw outputs are 1024² frames containing a subject that occupies a fraction of the canvas; downscaling that to 96² yields a creature ~20px tall floating in white.
_deviations.action: A trim-to-content step runs BEFORE step 1 for the sprite classes (declared per class as `postprocess.trim`), and the downscale then fits the trimmed subject into the target frame preserving aspect. §9.3's three named steps keep their order and their semantics; this is an addition, not a reordering. Maps and painted dex do not trim.

_deviations.finding: Two post-process target sizes named in §9.3 — battle 96² and mini 32² — have no home in data/balance.json, unlike the overworld character size (balance.map.playerSpriteW/H), the map size (balance.map.mapNativePx) and the prop scale (balance.map.propInteractionRadiusDefault).
_deviations.action: They ship as `targetW`/`targetH` on the class specs in this file, which is the art lane's data file. tests/unit/manifest.test.ts binds every class target that DOES have a balance source to that source, so the three sizes that are shared with the game can never drift; the two that are art-only are reviewable in one place. Raised for Lane A: `balance.map.battleSpritePx` and `balance.map.miniSpritePx` would close it.

_deviations.finding: Seven of the 35 dex identities have no concept text anywhere in the bible: Vulkindle, Pyrevane, Rillisk, Maelstrisk, Bramblore, Thornwald (the metamorphic starters' adult/elder identities) and — partially — Gloomgrub.
_deviations.action: Handled the way every other number the bible leaves open is handled: BY PUBLISHED RULE, not by taste. A form with no concept of its own inherits its line's bible concept plus its age stage ('grown to its adult form'). No new anatomy, colour or creature is invented; the entry records `derivedFrom` and its rule so a reviewer can audit it in one place. Gloomgrub's concept IS bible-sourced (§4 row 16 and the metamorphic paragraph: 'Poison/Plant grub').

_deviations.finding: L6 says the string `green shirt, ranger cap with star badge, leather satchel, walking boots` appears VERBATIM in every player prompt. The prompt that actually produced the gate-B0-approved sprite does not contain it verbatim — it elaborates: `a green shirt, brown shorts, a peaked green ranger cap with a small yellow star badge, a leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and brown walking boots`.
_deviations.action: The approved prompt wins, and this is why: §8.4 and G5 make an approved asset's prompt+seed its identity, and the approved sprite is the one Hank signed off at a SUPERVISED gate. Substituting the L6 string would generate a different character while claiming to be a regeneration — the exact failure G5 exists to prevent. Every L6 ELEMENT is present (green shirt · ranger cap · star badge · leather satchel · walking boots) and the cape ban is enforced on the negative side, so L6's intent holds; only its 'verbatim' clause does not. `_player.l6Verbatim` keeps the spec string on the record, and tests/unit/manifest.test.ts asserts the elements plus byte-equality with manifest-b0.json's approved row.

_deviations.finding: §9.2 says 'front-load and repeat distinctive anatomy (Fenmaw's gharial snout class of failure)'. The derivation did exactly that and Fenmaw STILL came back a generic crocodile — the subject already read `bulk gharial with a long narrow gharial snout` twice (assets/raw/palette-trials/pt-fenmaw.png). Repetition is not the missing piece: this model reads the SPECIES TERM `gharial` as its common relative `crocodile`, so repeating the term repeats the wrong animal. Confirmed by one generation per hypothesis: replacing the term with the SHAPE — `an extremely long thin tube-shaped snout, a narrow needle-like jaw far longer than the head is wide` — produced a true gharial (pt-fenmaw-b.png). The same collapse is visible in every other trial whose identity rests on a specialist term: `lungfish` rendered a generic bipedal fish blob (pt-mirefin.png), the `wyrm` of `spider-wyrm` vanished and left a plain spider (pt-webvern.png), `spore-antlered` rendered plain deer antlers (pt-sporantle.png), `eyeless` rendered a serpent with large eyes (pt-undermere.png), `will-o-wisp` rendered nothing at all (pt-wispurr.png), `dusk moth` rendered butterfly filaments (pt-gloomoth.png), `mudball tadpole` rendered a bipedal blob with no tail (pt-bogling.png).
_deviations.action: §9.2's fidelity rule gains a second clause, and `_concepts` is where it is applied: NAME DISTINCTIVE ANATOMY BY ITS SHAPE, NEVER BY ITS SPECIES TERM — the term stays (it is the bible's word and G2 protects it), the shape is added beside it and both are then front-loaded and repeated by the derivation. Rewritten: Fenmaw, Mirefin, Webvern, Sporantle, Undermere, Bogling, Wispurr, Gloomoth (each measured above) and Stonewing (reasoned, not measured — no trial exists). Deliberately NOT rewritten: Pyrelisk, because 'basilisk' fixes no anatomy in the bible and a shape restatement would have to invent one. THIS IS A PROMPT CHANGE, NOT A CONTENT CHANGE: every bible name, type, role, habitat and concept term is untouched and still appears verbatim in the subject; only the wording that steers the generator is added. Rewriting what Fenmaw IS would be a G2 violation; describing the gharial's snout by its geometry is a pipeline fidelity fix. Seeds are unaffected — `deriveSeed` is pure in (id, version), so no row's seed moves and G5 is not engaged.

map-town._skeletonSource: PROJECTION SUPERSEDED THIS SESSION. docs/TICKETS.md T-17 reads 'fix scale, keep isometric'; Hank overrode his own ruling, verbatim: "I was actually trying to match Gold when I said isometric, but if Gold is actually top down, then let's do top down" — and immediately after, "if that means that we can reintroduce the multi-level towns, that'd be really cool too. You can reference Ruby and Sapphire for that, I believe." So the isometric half of this skeleton is replaced by flat top-down in the gen-2 Gold idiom (assets/reference/gen2), and multi-level is back on, expressed the way a gen-3 top-down map expresses elevation — a band of rock lying flat across the ground (assets/reference/gen3) — and never as a side-on cutaway. This retires three of the nine rejects at the root: bowerdeep came back a floating island with an earth cross-section, cindershelf a side-on mine cutaway with no ground plane, sanctum a diorama on a plinth; all three were isometric trying to render vertical levels, and top-down cannot produce that failure. Conversely r5 carried a BLOCKING defect for being flat top-down — under this ruling that verdict is void and r5's projection was correct. || THE PROJECTION CLAUSE, and where it comes from. 'flat top-down view looking straight down onto the ground, every roof seen from above as one flat shape with only a narrow strip of front wall showing under its lower edge' is measured off the reference set: all 18 buildings in the four gen-2 towns show their roof as a flat shape from above, and all 18 doors are on the BOTTOM face, one 16 px tile wide, usually left of centre. 'the light coming from the upper left' is measured in every one of the five gen-2 captures — tree tiles are +15.6 to +20.6 luminance brighter in their top-left quadrant than their bottom-right, and building left edges are +10 to +14 brighter than their right edges. Together they replace 'chunky three-quarter isometric view ... one lit top face and two shaded side faces', which was the converging promptFix of the cindershelf, r4 and r5 reviewers and is now meaningless. || SCALE — THE MEASURED BAND, WHICH CORRECTS THE ONE THIS FILE WAS USING. The old bar was 85-140 native px, arrived at as 'about a twelfth of the picture'. Measured instead against the reference set (18 buildings over four gen-2 towns; there are exactly THREE footprints in the whole set and nothing between them — 64x32, 64x64 and 96x64 native px) and transferred by screen-fraction onto TROPHIC's 240 x 160 native play window (data/balance.json mapNativePx 1024, mapRenderScale 2, virtualWidth 480, virtualHeight 320): ordinary dwelling 96 wide x 48 deep; named landmark 96 x 71; the single largest civic building on the map 144 x 71; ceiling on depth 96. So the old bar was close to right for WIDTH and simply ABSENT for DEPTH — and depth is the worse axis (duskhollow's cottages came in 142-162 deep against a 160 px window). The 48 px depth is not the raw screen-fraction figure, which is 36; it is raised to the height of the player sprite (balance.json playerSpriteH 48), because a building cannot be shorter on screen than the player standing beside it. || WHY IT IS ANCHORED TO THE LANE. The lane is the one element the generator sizes correctly — measured in-band on five shipped maps (r1 track 58-87 px, r3 trail 50-85, r5 track 90-110, r2 boardwalk 52, brackwater planking 34) while every building and prop ran 130-355. Gold's own ratio is measured too: the bounded lane is 2 tiles / 32 native px in every reference town, an ordinary building is 2.0x that width and the Gym or Elm's Lab is 3.0x it. Transferred, the lane is 48 px and the ratios carry over unchanged. THE SHIPPED CLAUSE THIS REPLACES — 'nothing standing on the ground is wider or taller than that lane is wide' — was 2 to 3 times TIGHTER than Gold and would have produced buildings half the reference size if anything had ever obeyed it. || COMPOSITION, the number the twelve rejects were furthest from: a Gold town frame is a median 37% open walkable ground, 13.5% building footprint and 57% IMPASSABLE MASS — tree, water or cliff (per-town range 22-49 / 7.8-16.5 / 34-64). More than half the frame is terrain you cannot walk through and the built part is a clearing cut into it. It cannot ship as a fraction, because fractions of the frame are measured INERT (see _gate), so it ships as 'much of the picture taken up by a mass of trees, water or rock too thick to walk through, with the built ground a clearing cut into that mass'. This is also why the answer to a five-building hamlet on a 1024 square is MORE TERRAIN, not more buildings: Gold's density would imply 16-27 buildings here, which is exactly the ~50-house street grid R1 measured the enumerated subject killing. || WHAT WAS REMOVED AND WHY. (1) 'the ground between the buildings covered all over with many small things rather than a few large ones' is replaced by the motif clause. Measured: solid 5x5 single-colour patches cover 0.0-1.5% of a Gold frame, and its answer to a bare field is not scattered objects but a small repeating motif inside every 16 px tile (8-16 quantised colours per tile, repeating on a 16/32 px period — the strongest autocorrelation peaks in every reference town are lag 32 and lag 64). The dead zones the old clause was aimed at (brackwater 400x350 px of empty plaza, duskhollow 400x450 of empty blue) are now answered twice, by the motif and by the impassable mass. (2) 'regular chequerboard dithering in place of any gradient' is removed because the reference contradicts it outright: perfect 2-colour 2x2 checkerboards cover 0.55-0.89% of a Gold frame. Its intent survives as 'every gradient replaced by a hard step between two flat colours'. || WHAT IS NEW AND MEASURED: 'no pure black anywhere' and 'about two dozen colours' — the darkest pixel in any of the five gen-2 captures is luminance 57-58 of 255, the keyline is a 1 px dark neutral grey (#393939) on man-made objects and a dark green (#374432) on foliage, dark pixels are only 6.6-8.4% of a frame, and distinct colours per map run 21-38 with a median near 27. The door clause is measured (24 x 24 px transferred, a quarter of a 96 px building, bottom face, left of centre, all 18 of 18). The square-and-not-in-rows clause is measured: every reference building is axis-aligned on the 16 px lattice (16 of 18 on the 32 px one) and yet there is no street network, no crossroads and no shared street line anywhere in the five references — in New Bark no two buildings share an x or a y. || WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED, because it was measured to work: the full-bleed clause (0.06% void at assets/raw/_trials/map-fix-round/y1 against 13.6-31.1% on the shipped maps) minus the three words 'no cliff edge', which now forbid the exact device the multi-level ruling restores; the per-material colour separation clause; and the hard-pixel-edge tail. The style tail as a whole measured keyline ink 3.62% -> 4.67%, functionally-grayscale 2.54% -> 1.20%, void held at 0.23%. 'one single walkable ground level' becomes 'one continuous sheet of that same ground running under everything in the picture, the same sheet on both sides of every band of rock' — it has to permit a band without permitting stacked planes. || THE BAND is measured off assets/reference/gen3/lavaridge-town.png: the drop is a single band of dark rock drawn as a face along the south side of the higher ground, 12-15 native px thick at twelve sampled x positions — exactly one 16 px tile — its top line scalloped on a one-tile rhythm (dominant lobe period 16.4 native px, peak-to-trough up to 12 px) and its bottom line straight and hard, the face 1/4 to 1/2 the luminance of the surface and about 2.6x its saturation, with a ~3 px lit lip along the top. It is stated here as a third of the lane's width (16 px) rather than as a fifth of a building's depth: that is the same measurement expressed against gen-3's much deeper 80 px house, and against our 48 px house the two forms disagree — the lane is the anchor the generator obeys. || MAP-PROMPT-RULES R2 (the negative is inert at cfg 1.0) is why every clause here is positive; R4 is why the walkway is a 'lane, track or boardwalk' and never a road. || REGEN-V3 PASS — FIVE CLAUSES DELETED, EACH WITH ITS EVIDENCE. Do not reinstate any of them without a controlled cell that beats assets/raw/_trials/regen-v3. (1) THE CLIFF/STEP CLAUSE IS DELETED FROM ALL THREE MAP SKELETONS — town: 'where the ground steps up that step is drawn as one flat band of darker rock lying across the ground, about a third as deep from its top line to its bottom line as the lane is wide, its top line a row of rounded lobes and its bottom line straight and hard'; route: the same device as a short bar. EVIDENCE, a single-variable ablation at one seed (2278748833) in assets/raw/_trials/cause-hunt: w5-noneg-control (clause KEPT, every negation removed) came back with a full-width brown earth band across the BOTTOM FRAME EDGE; w6-nocliff-control (clause REMOVED, every negation kept) came back with none. In regen-v2 the band appears on 5 of 12 shipped picks and it SEALS the top and bottom edges of bowerdeep and r4, which is why those two generated ZERO edge exits against a declared two-exit adjacency. The clause was written for the three nodes that actually have elevation and it fired on the nine that do not. THE CAPABILITY IS NOT LOST: cindershelf, duskhollow and r4 each already carry their own band clause in _nodes[].feature, complete with the gap the path passes through, and bowerdeep and sanctum-approach never wanted a rock band at all (their elevation is a plank walk and a stone stair). The anti-cutaway invariant the band needs — 'the same sheet on both sides of every band of rock' — STAYS in all three skeletons. (2) THE IMPASSABLE-MASS CLAUSE IS DELETED FROM map-town — 'much of the picture taken up by a mass of trees, water or rock too thick to walk through, with the built ground a clearing cut into that mass'. EVIDENCE: it draws a RECTANGULAR TREE RING round the frame with the buildings pushed onto the perimeter and the interior left empty. brackwater and bowerdeep came back indistinguishable siblings under it — same green rectangle, same tree border, same empty middle — which is Hank's original complaint verbatim ('two of the three towns that were drafted look exceptionally similar to each other', EVAL-STANDARD §3 rule 9). It also overrode the ground each node names: bowerdeep asks for brown leaf litter over the whole picture and came back bright green grass, because a 'clearing cut into a mass' is a lawn. The CONTROL cell that beat all three new-skeleton Hearthollows (assets/raw/_trials/regen-v2/raw/CONTROL-hearthollow-oldprompt-s42.png, prompt at assets/raw/_trials/gold-recipe-nocn/_prompt.ts) carries NO mass clause and has no tree ring. The 57%-impassable measurement behind it stands; what does not stand is stating it in the CLASS, where it becomes the same rectangle twelve times. It is a per-node matter and every node already names its own terrain. (3) EVERY NEGATION IS GONE FROM ALL THREE SKELETONS, REPLACED BY AN AFFIRMATION. MAP-PROMPT-RULES R2 is about the NEGATIVE PROMPT being inert at cfg 1.0; a negation inside the POSITIVE prompt is not inert, it is tokenized, and 'none lined up in a regular grid or in repeated rows' had never once prevented a grid. The class has generated once, map-sanctum, and it was a REJECT: a hexagonal block of terrain floating on a plinth in blank cream, 31.1% of the canvas flat unpainted cream (rows y<260 are 47-97% cream), a Minecraft-style cutaway soil stratum around the whole rim and a drop shadow on the void — and the cohesion pass found it is the same construction as map-bowerdeep, which is Hank's look-alike complaint recurring between the opening town and the terminal site. THAT FAILURE IS ONE OF THE THREE THE PROJECTION CHANGE RETIRES AT THE ROOT: a plinth-and-cutaway diorama is what an isometric prompt does when it is asked for a bounded piece of ground, and a flat top-down view has no side faces to build a plinth out of. The full-bleed clause remains the other half of that defence and is the one clause here with trial evidence (assets/raw/_trials/map-fix-round y1 0.06% void, y3 0.02%). || The size ceiling is not trialled: the candidate that was, y4-sanctum-bleed-scale, left the stones at 117x181-197 against a shipped 110-118x188-207 and did not clear the cream either (30.0%) — and it did not, because it was a CAMERA-DISTANCE request, which is one of the two devices measured inert. Both are recorded in full at classes['map-town']._gate and neither may be added here. || FIRST CHECKS, in order: is the ring a circle rather than an ellipse; is the grazed interior legible against the knee-high grass outside it; is the stone width at or under 2.0x the footpath width (ratio first, absolute px second); and is native (512,512) inside the ring on open grass, which is where chooseSpawnTile puts the player on every arrival. || REGEN-V3 — WHAT TO CHECK FIRST, in order. (a) IS THE BAND GONE FROM THE FRAME EDGE. It is the defect deletion (1) is aimed at and the one that cost most; measure the top and bottom 32 rows against the interior before looking at anything else. (b) DO bowerdeep AND r4 HAVE TWO EDGE EXITS each. Both had zero in regen-v2 and the band sealing their top and bottom edges is the stated cause; if they still have zero the cause was misdiagnosed and the next suspect is the node's own wording, not the class. (c) DO brackwater AND bowerdeep STILL READ AS SIBLINGS. That is deletion (2)'s whole purpose and it is EVAL-STANDARD §3 rule 9, the half of Hank's critique that actually bites. (d) IS THERE STILL A GRID. With the negation converted to an affirmation, a grid now means the affirmation is too weak rather than that the model ignored a prohibition. (e) HAS ANYTHING THE DELETED CLAUSES WERE HOLDING BACK RETURNED — void or a border at the frame edge (the full-bleed affirmation now carries that alone), a bare single-colour field where the tree mass used to be (the motif clause and the node's own scatter now carry that alone), a person, a building on a route, or blur. Each of those is a REGRESSION traceable to a named deletion and each is reinstated by rewriting that one clause as an affirmation, never by restoring the negation.
map-site.skeleton: pixel art top-down map, retro 90s handheld RPG style, {subject}, flat top-down view looking straight down onto the ground, no view from the horizon, every standing stone, rock and tree crown seen from above as one flat shape with only a narrow strip of its front face showing under its lower edge, the light coming from the upper left so the upper-left side of each of them is the lighter side and its lower-right side the darker one, the ground named here covers the entire picture and runs off all four sides of it, one continuous sheet of that same ground running under everything in the picture, the same sheet on both sides of every band of rock, with no island, no plinth, no cutaway earth wall, no border and no blank background anywhere, that ground reaching the outermost row of pixels on all four sides of the picture and carrying on past every one of them, the footpath is about forty-eight pixels from one side of it to the other and it sets the size of everything else: a standing stone is about as wide as that footpath and at most twice as wide, and everything standing on the ground reaches at most twice the footpath's width from its far edge to its near edge, everything set square to the picture with its edges parallel to the sides of it, the ground around them carrying the same small repeating motif of specks and tufts all over it, the walkable ground, the grass, the stone and the grit each keeping their own colour so the ground can be told at a glance from what stands on it, flat blocks of solid colour from a small fixed palette of about two dozen colours, the darkest of them a dark neutral grey, every shape ringed by a hard one-pixel keyline, dark grey on stone and dark green on leaves, every gradient replaced by a hard step between two flat colours, every edge a hard pixel step, 2D game asset
map-site._skeletonSource: PROJECTION SUPERSEDED THIS SESSION. docs/TICKETS.md T-17 reads 'fix scale, keep isometric'; Hank overrode his own ruling, verbatim: "I was actually trying to match Gold when I said isometric, but if Gold is actually top down, then let's do top down" — and immediately after, "if that means that we can reintroduce the multi-level towns, that'd be really cool too. You can reference Ruby and Sapphire for that, I believe." So the isometric half of this skeleton is replaced by flat top-down in the gen-2 Gold idiom (assets/reference/gen2), and multi-level is back on, expressed the way a gen-3 top-down map expresses elevation — a band of rock lying flat across the ground (assets/reference/gen3) — and never as a side-on cutaway. This retires three of the nine rejects at the root: bowerdeep came back a floating island with an earth cross-section, cindershelf a side-on mine cutaway with no ground plane, sanctum a diorama on a plinth; all three were isometric trying to render vertical levels, and top-down cannot produce that failure. Conversely r5 carried a BLOCKING defect for being flat top-down — under this ruling that verdict is void and r5's projection was correct. || This class is still map-town's skeleton minus every buildings clause and map-route's minus 'no buildings' — a site is a place that is neither a settlement nor a road — and it takes the same rewrite: flat top-down projection with a narrow strip of front face under each shape's lower edge, upper-left light, the full-bleed clause minus 'no cliff edge', the motif clause in place of 'many small things', 'every gradient replaced by a hard step' in place of chequerboard dither, the no-pure-black and two-dozen-colour findings, and a footpath-anchored size ceiling loosened from 1.0x to 2.0x the path's width by measurement. All of those measurements are recorded once, at classes['map-town']._skeletonSource. || WHAT THE PROJECTION CHANGE RESOLVES HERE, specifically. The old _gate recorded a real tension: the ceiling bounded the stones' HEIGHT to the footpath's width rather than to the stone's own width, because the Sanctum's stones are authored 'tall' and 'no taller than it is wide' would have fought the bible. Seen from directly above, a standing stone has no drawn height at all — it has a width, a depth from its far edge to its near edge, and a narrow strip of front face. 'Tall' becomes a content word rather than a picture dimension, and the ceiling can now be stated on both drawn axes without inverting any silhouette, because there is no silhouette to invert. || The nine-stone ring is also strictly better off overhead: the ring reads as a circle with the grazed interior open inside it, where a three-quarter view foreshortens that circle into an ellipse and hides the far side of the grass behind the near stones — and the grazed interior is the picture's one piece of evidence of the Vellsire (prop.sanctum-antler-ring). MAP-PROMPT-RULES R2 is why every clause is positive. || REGEN-V3 PASS — FIVE CLAUSES DELETED, EACH WITH ITS EVIDENCE. Do not reinstate any of them without a controlled cell that beats assets/raw/_trials/regen-v3. (1) THE CLIFF/STEP CLAUSE IS DELETED FROM ALL THREE MAP SKELETONS — town: 'where the ground steps up that step is drawn as one flat band of darker rock lying across the ground, about a third as deep from its top line to its bottom line as the lane is wide, its top line a row of rounded lobes and its bottom line straight and hard'; route: the same device as a short bar. EVIDENCE, a single-variable ablation at one seed (2278748833) in assets/raw/_trials/cause-hunt: w5-noneg-control (clause KEPT, every negation removed) came back with a full-width brown earth band across the BOTTOM FRAME EDGE; w6-nocliff-control (clause REMOVED, every negation kept) came back with none. In regen-v2 the band appears on 5 of 12 shipped picks and it SEALS the top and bottom edges of bowerdeep and r4, which is why those two generated ZERO edge exits against a declared two-exit adjacency. The clause was written for the three nodes that actually have elevation and it fired on the nine that do not. THE CAPABILITY IS NOT LOST: cindershelf, duskhollow and r4 each already carry their own band clause in _nodes[].feature, complete with the gap the path passes through, and bowerdeep and sanctum-approach never wanted a rock band at all (their elevation is a plank walk and a stone stair). The anti-cutaway invariant the band needs — 'the same sheet on both sides of every band of rock' — STAYS in all three skeletons. (2) THE IMPASSABLE-MASS CLAUSE IS DELETED FROM map-town — 'much of the picture taken up by a mass of trees, water or rock too thick to walk through, with the built ground a clearing cut into that mass'. EVIDENCE: it draws a RECTANGULAR TREE RING round the frame with the buildings pushed onto the perimeter and the interior left empty. brackwater and bowerdeep came back indistinguishable siblings under it — same green rectangle, same tree border, same empty middle — which is Hank's original complaint verbatim ('two of the three towns that were drafted look exceptionally similar to each other', EVAL-STANDARD §3 rule 9). It also overrode the ground each node names: bowerdeep asks for brown leaf litter over the whole picture and came back bright green grass, because a 'clearing cut into a mass' is a lawn. The CONTROL cell that beat all three new-skeleton Hearthollows (assets/raw/_trials/regen-v2/raw/CONTROL-hearthollow-oldprompt-s42.png, prompt at assets/raw/_trials/gold-recipe-nocn/_prompt.ts) carries NO mass clause and has no tree ring. The 57%-impassable measurement behind it stands; what does not stand is stating it in the CLASS, where it becomes the same rectangle twelve times. It is a per-node matter and every node already names its own terrain. (3) EVERY NEGATION IS GONE FROM ALL THREE SKELETONS, REPLACED BY AN AFFIRMATION. MAP-PROMPT-RULES R2 is about the NEGATIVE PROMPT being inert at cfg 1.0; a negation inside the POSITIVE prompt is not inert, it is tokenized, and 'none lined up in a regular grid or in repeated rows' had never once prevented a grid. Converted: 'no characters' -> deleted (w5 dropped it and no person appeared); 'no buildings' (route) -> 'the picture holding only ground, plants, rock and water' — the old form was already recorded here as KNOWN INSUFFICIENT, and no building appeared anywhere in regen-v2; 'none turned at an angle and none lined up in a regular grid or in repeated rows' -> 'the buildings scattered at uneven spacing, some standing close together in twos and threes and others well apart, each one at its own distance from the lane so that each stands on a line of its own'; 'nothing built reaches further ... than' -> 'everything built reaches at most'; 'never more than twice as wide' -> 'at most twice as wide'; 'only ever ... and never one object' -> the plain positive; 'never a flat field of one colour but carrying' -> 'carrying'; 'no shape turned at an angle' -> 'its edges parallel to the sides of it'; 'and no pure black anywhere' -> 'the darkest of them a dark neutral grey'; 'with no blur and no airbrush shading' -> deleted. w5-noneg-control is the evidence that stripping the style-tail negations costs nothing: it is hard-pixelled, unblurred and full-bleed without them. NOTE, so it is not misread later: w5 rewrote six negations as affirmations AND THE EARTH BAND SURVIVED. That is not evidence that affirmations do not work — w5 was testing a different defect, and the band's cause is (1). || CORRECTION, MEASURED, WITHIN THIS SAME PASS — THE FULL-BLEED NEGATIONS ARE NOT INERT AND ARE RESTORED VERBATIM. The first regen-v3 batch was run with 'with no island, no plinth, no cutaway earth wall, no border and no blank background anywhere' DELETED from all three skeletons and replaced by the affirmation alone. It came back as the framed-island failure: the map painted as a green square floating on a flat neutral matte with cut corners. Measured over the 26 cells of that batch (assets/raw/_trials/regen-v3/_ablation-nonegations/, kept as the record) by mean chroma in the outer 16 px ring against the 624x624 core: EIGHT cells read ring chroma under 12 and under 0.45x their own core — hearthollow 3 of 3 (1.9/116, 4.5/122, 8.9/122), brackwater 3 of 3, cindershelf 3 of 3, r4 2 of 3 — against TWO of 37 by the identical measure on regen-v2, where hearthollow and brackwater were 0 of 3 each. The affirmation alone does not hold the frame. So the negations are restored and the affirmation is KEPT BESIDE THEM. The general rule this establishes, now written into tools/comfy/MAP-PROMPT-RULES.md under R2: R2 is about the `negative` FIELD, which cfg 1.0 never evaluates; a negated phrase inside the POSITIVE prompt is an ordinary token sequence and works or does not work on its own evidence. 'none lined up in a regular grid or in repeated rows' is still fairly deleted — not because it is a negation but because a grid kept appearing under it. Never delete a positive-prompt clause for its grammar. || SECOND MEASURED CONSEQUENCE OF DELETING THE IMPASSABLE-MASS CLAUSE, recorded so it is not rediscovered: that clause was also the only thing bounding the BUILT AREA of a town. With it gone and no building count in the node string, bowerdeep came back with 22 near-identical dark-roofed huts on a rectangular boardwalk ring (_ablation-nonegations/bowerdeep-s42.png) — EVAL-STANDARD §3 rules 7, 8 and 9 all at once. The answer is R1's, not the mass clause's: the count goes in the node enumeration (bowerdeep and cindershelf both carried none and both now say 'five buildings'), and the class gains one affirmative distinctness clause, 'every building in the picture a different size and a different shape from every other one'. That wording deliberately does NOT say 'a different roof colour', because the gen-2 measurement recorded at _nodes.hearthollow.featureSource finds one roof colour per town. || REGEN-V4 — 'no view from the horizon' RESTORED HERE, AND MEASURED INERT FOR THE DEFECT IT WAS RESTORED AGAINST. The phrase is verbatim from the old control prompt's PROJECTION clause (assets/raw/_trials/gold-recipe-nocn/_prompt.ts) and was restored because duskhollow painted a solid blue sky band along the TOP FRAME EDGE in all three regen-v3 seeds — a horizon in a top-down map, which is a blank background at the frame edge and eats the top exit — while the old control prompt carried the phrase and did not do it. THE CORRELATION WAS FALSE. Single-variable, LoRA off, seed 7: share of the top 48 rows that is saturated blue (B-R>40 and B-G>25) reads 99.53% under the old skeleton and 99.61% under the restored clause. The clause moved it by 0.08 points. THE ACTUAL CAUSE IS IN THE NODE STRING and a class clause cannot reach it — see _nodes.duskhollow.featureSource, where removing 'and all of it under a cold blue twilight' takes the same measure from 99.61% to 0.00%. The phrase is LEFT IN because assets/raw/_trials/regen-v4's twenty-four LoRA cells were generated under it and removing it now would make them unreproducible from this manifest — the exact provenance hole regen-v3 opened. It is a fair candidate for deletion under MAP-PROMPT-RULES R2's 'delete it only when measured inert', but that deletion is a deliberate act and needs its own controlled cell, because inert against the sky band is not the same as inert.

hearthollow.feature: on close-cropped green turf and packed brown earth: a farming hamlet of five buildings set well apart around one open grazing green, the turf running out to all four sides of the picture, Warden Maren's timber field station under a shallow plank roof, a fenced specimen pen and drying racks beside it; a stone-walled gym hall under a steep mossy slate roof, its shed and fenced yard at the foot of the green; a long low inn with a byre; a supply shop with a green awning over its door and an open bait crate outside it; and a deep-thatched cottage between a bare fallow field and standing barley; empty cropped turf with nothing built on it at the exact middle of the picture where a worn dirt lane forks, a plain blank survey board on a short post just below the middle, its face bare weathered timber; wildflower clumps, grass tufts and a few round oaks cover the open ground between the buildings so that no stretch of it is left bare, one thick hedgerow behind the cottage; the lane climbs out through a timber field gate at the top and goes on to the Meadow Reach
hearthollow.featureSource: ORGANISING IDEA (five buildings standing well apart around one open grazing green, joined by a forking dirt lane) — 'the green' is a shipped place, and the UNCONDITIONAL source is maribel.post.win (when {}) 'Come the turn of the year the whole green goes up in lanterns'. maren.greeting.act1 'Maribel keeps the gym at the bottom of the green' is MAREN's line, not Maribel's (transcription slip in the previous pass, corrected here), and it is CONDITIONAL — when {act:[1], floraStock r1 ≥ 46} — so it is cited for placement only, on top of the unconditional line. festival.hearthollow 'The lanterns are up on the green' is flag-gated on event.festival.open, so it is corroboration, not base state. || TOP-DOWN (T-17's 'keep isometric' is SUPERSEDED this session — see classes['map-town']._skeletonSource for the ruling): roof PITCH is invisible from directly overhead, so the two pitch words are cut from the painted string ('shallow plank roof' -> 'plank roof', 'steep mossy slate roof' -> 'mossy slate roof') and the separating work falls on roof COLOUR and MATERIAL and on footprint, which is what a flat overhead view actually shows — plank / mossy slate / byre-ended inn / awning / deep thatch. Roof and wall materials are art choices in the R7 'concrete structure' class, not named content; the slate and the stone walls are carried from the passing cell assets/raw/_trials/map-town-style/t4-skelA-mapneg. || field station + fenced specimen pen — bible §6 row 1 'Warden Maren's field station'; the pen from maren.opening 'Three in the pen behind you' (act-0 opening cutscene, i.e. the first thing the player sees). Drying racks from the t4 cell. NOT sourced to maren.retirement's 'the run of the yard' — that entry is when {yearMin 2, …}. || gym hall AT THE FOOT OF THE GREEN — data/gyms.json maribel.town='hearthollow'; placement from maren.greeting.act1 as above. Its shed and yard are UNCONDITIONAL: maribel.greeting (when {}) 'I'm in and out of the shed all morning' and maribel.post.loss (when {}) 'she'll stop out on the yard tonight'. || inn with a byre — innkeeper-hearthollow.rest (when {}) 'Your animals are in the byre with the door shut'. || SUPPLY SHOP, not a bait shop — vendor-hearthollow.shop (when {}) 'Snares and salve. Tonic's behind me and it costs what it costs' and 'Bait's in the crate by your knee, not sorted, so dig'. Kett runs the town's GENERAL store — snares, salve, tonic AND bait — matching bible §11's sinks. The previous pass's 'bait shop' invented a specialised business and lost the snare/medicine sink; the open bait crate keeps the shipped detail without inventing the business. The green awning is an art colour choice, unsourced, carried from the first draft. || fallow field + standing barley — tolm.greeting (when {}) 'Four fields, and one of them lies fallow every year … It's the west field this year'; barley from maribel.greeting (when {}) 'The other got through the hedge into the barley after the Loamunder'. Bible §9 'The Fallow Field'. Painted as ONE fallow field and ONE barley strip, not four fields, because a four-field enumeration is the field-grid failure R5/R8 measured at round3/v4-r1. || SURVEY BOARD on a post — prop hearthollow-signpost, kind sign-card, x512 y648, label 'Warden Maren's field station'; prop text (when {}) 'FIELD STATION — HEARTHOLLOW. Survey sheets go up at first light. Pencil and blanks in the tin by the door.' Called a SURVEY board rather than a notice board for two reasons: it is better sourced (maren.greeting.hearthollow, when {}, 'This morning's numbers are up on the board'), and it removes the last phrase this town shared with Duskhollow, whose own board is 'a torn notice board on a post'. x512/y648 is on the centre line and 136 px BELOW centre, which is exactly what 'just below' paints, and it is off the spawn tile. || hedgerow — from tools/comfy/manifest.json _nodes.r1.feature 'an open meadow reach of grass and hedgerows', and corroborated unconditionally in town by maribel.greeting 'got through the hedge into the barley' and amb.hearthollow-elder.base 'the Skir come over the hedge at dusk'. NOT from the bible — `grep -n hedge docs/content-bible.md` returns only line 88 'bramble hedgehog'; the previous pass's bible §6 citation for hedgerows was false. R3 FIX: the hedgerow is now ONE placed object behind ONE building. The previous 'hedgerow … elsewhere' + 'field gate in the hedge at the top' reconstructed round2/u1-town-single-exit, which produced a rectangular hedge boundary round the whole town and a grid of paths inside it. Nothing is now said about what any edge of the frame holds. || timber field gate at the top — prop.hearthollow-signpost (when {}) 'north gate for the Reach'; tolm.greeting (when {}) 'Mind the gate — lift and shove together or it stops dead'. Destination 'the Meadow Reach' = data/nodes/r1.json name, bible §6 routes row. || EXIT CONTRACT: adjacency ['r1'] — ONE exit, at the TOP (convention: top = on toward the Sanctum). No other edge described (R3). || CENTRE: 'empty cropped turf at the exact middle of the picture … nothing built on it' — native (512,512) is standable green. This is the explicit repair of t4, where a stone building landed on the centre. || SCALE: no size clause here — the map-town skeleton carries the measured band, and the phrase this node used to be measured against, 'no wider than about a twelfth of the picture', is now recorded as MEASURED INERT at classes['map-town']._gate. || TENSION RECORDED, NOT RESOLVED: the gen-2 reference measurement finds that within one Gold town every roof shares ONE colour and ONE construction, and a landmark is marked by a larger footprint and a name plate rather than by different architecture — 18 buildings over four towns, three footprints in the whole set (64x32, 64x64, 96x64 native) and no fourth. Five different roofs is the opposite of that. It is kept because R1 measured the enumerated five-building subject to be the lever that turned a ~50-house street grid into a hamlet. If the first supervised top-down run comes back reading as five unrelated buildings, the Gold answer is one roof colour across the four ordinary buildings and a larger footprint on the gym hall. || REGEN-V3 — RESTORING WHAT THE OLDER PROMPT DID BETTER. The control cell (assets/raw/_trials/regen-v2/raw/CONTROL-hearthollow-oldprompt-s42.png, from assets/raw/_trials/gold-recipe-nocn/_prompt.ts) beat all three new-skeleton seeds on distinct buildings, on a blank sign and on ground that is not bare. Three things it said that this entry had lost, restored here: (1) THE GROUND MATERIAL. The old string ended 'Meadow biome, ground of close-cropped green turf and packed brown earth'; this entry ended at the biome word and named no material at all, which is the same R6 failure that put Brackwater's stilt houses on grass. It now LEADS with the ground. (2) THE FILLER LINE. 'wildflower clumps, grass tufts and a few round oaks cover the open ground between the buildings so no stretch of it is left bare' had been compressed to 'wildflower meadow and a few oaks on the open ground', which stopped answering EVAL-STANDARD §1 rule 5's dead zones. It is restored close to verbatim, and it matters more now that the class impassable-mass clause is deleted. (3) 'A PLAIN BLANK ... SIGN BOARD ON A SHORT POST'. One narrow trodden trail threads from the foot of the picture to the top, doubling back on itself twice where the ground steepens, running down toward the canopy town at the bottom and climbing onto bare stony ground at the top toward the ash country. cindershelf.feature: a mining town of five buildings on open black ash: black volcanic ash, cracked basalt, steam vents and glowing orange fissures and no grass anywhere over the whole picture, ore-cart rails laid flat across the ash; one band of dark red-brown rock lies across the ash a little above the middle of the picture, its ends stopping well short of both sides of it, its top line a row of rounded lobes and its bottom line straight and hard, the rock in it far darker and far more strongly coloured than the ash on either side of it with a thin lit strip of paler rock along its very top, and the same ash carries on above the band and below it; on the near side of the band a relic forge with a tall smoking chimney and a glowing forge mouth, a small squat gym forge of dark basalt block a short way off across the ash with a black slag heap between the two, and left of the middle a timbered shaft head with winch and ore carts over a dark shaft mouth, and beside it, level with the middle, a low shrine of curved fired plates fitted without mortar, candles burnt into hollows along the joins; lower and right of the middle a second timbered ladder head down into the deep workings; on the far side of the band and standing well clear of it, an inn with steaming stone bathing tubs outside it, a supply shop under a soot-stained awning, and a boarded-up company store next door to the shop with its windows nailed over; a flight of wide cut stone steps is set into a gap in the band, drawn as eight short pale bars one above the next with a dark line under each bar, the ash on both sides of the gap running straight into the steps and the ore-cart rail passing through the same gap; bare flat ash with nothing built on it and no band crossing it at the exact middle of the picture between the shaft head and the forge; a cinder track leaves at the bottom for the Bowerdeep Wilds, and from the far ash the way climbs on at the top onto the Cinder Steppe
cindershelf.featureSource: ORGANISING IDEA — TWO LEVELS AGAIN, ONE BAND BETWEEN THEM. Two flats of black ash, one lying above the other in the picture, divided by a single band of dark rock with a flight of cut stone steps and the ore-cart rail passing through one gap in it. This RESTORES the levels that were cut this morning, by Hank's later ruling of the same session, verbatim: "I was actually trying to match Gold when I said isometric, but if Gold is actually top down, then let's do top down" and "if that means that we can reintroduce the multi-level towns, that'd be really cool too. You can reference Ruby and Sapphire for that, I believe." docs/TICKETS.md T-17's 'keep isometric' is superseded with it. || WHY THE FLATTENING HAPPENED AND WHY IT IS NOW THE WRONG FIX. tools/artverify returned REJECT on the first generated cindershelf map: it came back as "a SIDE-ON MINE CUTAWAY: three horizontal shelves stacked one above the other in the picture plane, every building drawn in flat front elevation ... There is no ground plane anywhere in the image — not one surface recedes, no roof shows two faces, no terrace shows its floor", which the reviewer called "a platformer level cross-section, not Cindershelf". (That verdict came from the review run over the 12 maps and was never written to a file, so it is transcribed here rather than cited to a path.) A cross-section is a SIDE ELEVATION, and a flat top-down view has no side elevation to fall into — the failure was isometry trying to render vertical levels, not the levels themselves. So the levels come back and what is removed instead is the ABSTRACT ALTITUDE LANGUAGE the reviewer's own promptFix named: "The phrase 'on cut basalt benches at different heights down one ash scarp, joined by stone stairs and ore-cart rails' is what produces the cross-section". Nothing in this string now names a height, a level, a bench, a terrace or a scarp. It names marks to paint. || THE BAND IS MEASURED off assets/reference/gen3/lavaridge-town.png. A vertical face-pixel scan at twelve x positions along its north wall gives 12, 8, 14, 15, 12, 8, 13, 12, 14, 15, 14, 14 native px — exactly one 16 px tile, softened at the scalloped top edge. A frequency sweep of the topmost face-pixel row over x=330..620 gives a dominant lobe period of 16.4 native px with peak-to-trough amplitude up to 12 px, and the band's LOWER line is straight and hard. A column trace at native x=20 reads pale rock surface (luminance 153-167), then face (39-70), then a 2 px lit lip, then face again on a repeating 16 px step — which is the 'thin lit strip of paler rock along its very top'. Face core RGB (96,16,0)-(128,48,32) against surface (208,152,136)-(184,128,112): same hue family, a quarter to a half the luminance, about 2.6x the saturation. That is the whole of what 'far darker and far more strongly coloured' encodes. The band's DEPTH is not restated here; the map-town skeleton carries it as a third of the lane's width. || THE BRIEF'S LAVARIDGE PREMISE IS WRONG AND THIS STRING GOES BEYOND THE REFERENCE — RECORDED, NOT HIDDEN. Lavaridge does not show buildings standing on terraces at different heights: a tile-occupancy reclassification puts mountain at 0.1% of its interior 14x13-tile block, the rock is a 2-tile strip down the west edge and along the north edge, and all five of its buildings stand on ONE flat sheet. What Lavaridge supplies is the band VOCABULARY, not a terraced composition. Putting three buildings on the far side of a band while five other structures stand on the near side is an extrapolation from a map margin into a map interior, it is demonstrated by no image in assets/reference, and it is the single most likely thing in this pass to come back wrong. classes['map-town']._gate lists it as check (e). || THE STEPS ARE THE OTHER UNTRIALLED CLAUSE. Its named failure mode is a flat vertical rung-ladder in front elevation, which is exactly the shape this node's own blocking defect already recorded. GO UP and look at the shrine at the shaft head' and bram.warm.2 'You got UP to the shrine, then' — CHECKED, and they still hold as IDIOM rather than as literal elevation, exactly as before: the shrine prop cindershelf-shrine-mine sits at native (372,508), 140 px left of centre and 4 px ABOVE it, i.e. on the same ash as the spawn tile, and no band crosses between them. Putting the shaft head up on the far ash to make 'up' literal was drafted again this pass and cut again for the same mechanical reason: the player has to stand within 48 px of the hotspot, and moving it across a band risks the collision mask. sable.greeting (when {}) 'Colder up there than down here' — CHECKED, non-binding: 'up there' is the Cinder Steppe (r4), off this map at the top exit, the same use as maren.greeting.act4's 'Nine months since I was up there myself'. bram.greeting (when {}) 'Mind your feet that side. It earns its place twice over — it is an R7 concrete non-building structure, and it is the shipped line that puts the two forges apart HORIZONTALLY, which is the work the removed benches used to do. || inn with steaming stone bathing tubs — innkeeper-cindershelf.rest (when {}) 'There's a tub going now, and the tubs fill straight off the hot spring'. || supply shop under a soot-stained awning, and the boarded-up company store next to it — vendor-cindershelf.shop (when {}) 'My prices went up the month next door boarded its windows'. This is the shipped read of bible §6 row 4 'arrival mid-collapse'. || SHAFT. The unconditional grounding is gerta.greeting (when {}) 'One reading a shift, off the wall of the third shaft, thirty-one years of it' and amb.cindershelf-shafthand.base (when {}), which also ships 'Nobody has got round to the loose bit down by the winch' — the winch. bram.mine.expanding and bram.mine.closing stay dropped: their whens are {yearMin 5, r4 cragmar-line >= 12} and {yearMin 5, <= 3}, mutually exclusive year-variant states, neither true in the base year this map paints. 'over a dark adit' is now 'over a dark shaft mouth': a winch and a headframe stand over a VERTICAL shaft, which is what every shipped line describes ('Six days in seven I'm down it', 'below the shaft', 'got down to the deep shrine'), and an adit is a horizontal drift that has to be cut into a rock face — i.e. it was quietly asking for the scarp back. || CENTRE: 'bare flat ash with nothing built on it and no band crossing it at the exact middle of the picture between the shaft head and the forge'. r4.feature: mostly black ash: open volcanic steppe of black ash flats and cracked basalt, steaming vents, thin glowing orange fissures, loose cinder blocks and dry ash-grey scrub tufts, everything on this ground low and small, and no green grass anywhere. One thin ash path runs almost straight up the picture, jinking only where it steps round a vent, a disused narrow rail line, coiled cable and open wooden crates left along it and one heavy abandoned rail lying near the top; the path crosses the exact middle of the picture on packed ash with nothing on it, drops toward the forge town at the bottom, and climbs a low basalt scarp above the middle of the picture, drawn as one band of dark rock lying flat across the ash with its top line a row of rounded lobes and its bottom line straight and hard, the ash exactly the same colour above the band and below it, the path passing through a gap cut straight through that band and carrying on over open ash beyond it and out at the top toward the dark vale. Above and right of the middle a granite antler stone stands beside a steaming vent, windward face glazed to a skin of crazed lifting glass, sheltered face cut sharp
r4.featureSource: GROUND — 'black ash flats and cracked basalt … no green grass anywhere' is R6 applied verbatim in spirit: the exact clause that turned Cindershelf's two-volcanoes-on-a-lawn into basalt, ash, steam vents and orange fissures (palette-trials/pt-map-cindershelf vs round3/v2-cindershelf). Biome = data/nodes/r4.json Steppe + bible §6 routes 'R4 Cinder Steppe'. 'ash path' is one of R4's approved substitutes for the banned word. || SCALE COUNTER: 'everything on this ground low and small' — phrased for a treeless biome where the offenders are cinder blocks and scrub tufts rather than trees. Unlike the other five routes' wording. || PATH SHAPE, unique to this route: 'runs almost straight up the picture … jinking only where it steps round a vent'. This is the one route whose path is nearly straight, and it is earned rather than lazy — amb.r4-worker.base (when {}) says 'You can follow the cable runs the whole way up from the vent line', a single continuous run up the scarp. It is deliberately the opposite of r3's doubling-back and r5's kinking. || TOP-DOWN (T-17's 'keep isometric' is SUPERSEDED this session — see classes['map-town']._skeletonSource for the ruling): the scarp is now drawn the way gen-3 Lavaridge draws a level change from directly above — one band of dark rock lying flat across the ash, top line scalloped on a one-tile rhythm, bottom line straight and hard — and that is the only change to the painted string. Vents standing proud and a rail running up a grade are not renderable as relief from overhead; they render as their own top faces on the ash, which is enough. The scarp is still the top-end marker and is still dialogue-sourced (amb.r4-worker.base, amb.cindershelf-worker.base 'West scarp crew'). THE WORD 'scarp' IS DELIBERATELY KEPT even though the cindershelf reviewer named abstract altitude as the cause of that node's cross-section: what the reviewer indicted was 'down one ash scarp' — a phrase stating the world's vertical geometry with nothing to paint — whereas here the noun is dialogue-sourced and is immediately followed by the mark to paint. If the first supervised run comes back with a side-on rock face at the top of this frame, the word is what to cut, not the band. || INDUSTRIAL LEAVINGS, all from amb.r4-worker.base, which is UNCONDITIONAL (when {}): 'The lid's off that crate — they come open on their own'; 'Contract's shut, so I'm pulling cable and rail out'; 'There's a rail up top that four of us couldn't shift. sanctum.feature: mostly short grazed grass and pale volcanic grit: a ring of nine tall grey standing stones at the middle of the picture, evenly spaced, every one facing in toward the centre, each carved with a single antlered stag on its own, cut deep and large on the face; inside the ring the grass is grazed short and even, and the exact middle of the picture is open grazed grass with nothing standing on it, while outside the ring the grass stands knee high everywhere; fallen slabs, dry heather and a few dead trees on the wide flat floor around it; one worn footpath climbs in at the bottom through a tall gate standing open in a face of cut dark rock, comes up to the ring and enters it through a gap between two stones
sanctum.featureSource: CLASS CHANGE IS THE REAL FIX — tools/comfy/manifest.json _nodes.sanctum.kind is 'town', so this string previously composed into the map-town skeleton, which mandates buildings with doors. The Sanctum has none (bible §6 row 6: 'Sealed caldera | league + finale; no shops, one long approach'), and nothing in bible §6/§7/§9/§10/§11 or data/dialogue.json names a building, hall or structure there — not even for Greaves, who is data/gyms.json town 'sanctum'. No subject wording can beat a skeleton clause that mandates buildings, so this node is routed to the new map-site class instead. That also removes the R2 violation: the previous opening, 'not a town and no houses, shops or market anywhere', was NEGATION INSIDE THE POSITIVE PROMPT on a cfg-1.0 graph. R2's finding is that the NEGATIVE conditioning is never evaluated; it is emphatically not a finding that positive-prompt negation works, and naming houses, shops and a market in positive conditioning is the surest way to summon them — R6's mechanism running in reverse. Handled by class, so nothing has to be suppressed in words. || R3 + R5 VIOLATION REMOVED — the previous 'a wide flat floor … held inside a steep dark rock wall' was a containment instruction describing a boundary enclosing the whole frame (R3) and it implicitly demanded the entire caldera bowl fit in shot, which is R5's measured failure ('seen from very high above so the whole marsh fits in the frame at once' → a rectangular causeway grid). The rock now survives only as the local FACE the gate is cut into, which is what the shipped text actually supports: prop.sanctum-approach-antler-gate 'It is set into cut rock rather than into ground.' || NINE STONES, EVENLY SPACED, ALL FACING IN — prop.sanctum-antler-ring opens verbatim: 'Nine stones at the caldera heart, evenly spaced, every one facing in toward the middle.' R1 makes the enumeration the whole lever, and the previous string threw away a shipped number and a shipped orientation by saying only 'a ring of tall grey standing stones'. Restored. || THE CARVING IS RELATIVE, NOT ABSOLUTE — same prop text: 'Each stone carries one animal on its own, cut to double the size of the figures on the stones outside.' That is double the size of the SIX-FIGURE HERD carvings on the other antler stones, a relative measure against small carvings. The previous 'at twice life size' was a fabricated absolute and would render a stag larger than the stone it is cut into. It is now 'a single antlered stag on its own, cut deep and large on the face'. Antlered stag = the Vellsire: sanctum.vellsire.approach 'The branching on its antlers is the branching cut on every stone from Meadow Reach up to here.' || THE GRASS CONTRAST IS THE ONLY VISIBLE TRACE OF THE VELLSIRE, and the previous string erased it by painting 'thin fallow grass' everywhere. Same prop text: 'The grass inside the ring is short and even. The grass elsewhere in the Sanctum Fallow stands to the knee. Inside the ring it has been grazed down level.' Both halves are now in the picture, and the contrast between them is the picture's one piece of evidence. || TOP-DOWN (T-17's 'keep isometric' is SUPERSEDED this session — see classes['map-town']._skeletonSource for the ruling): nine standing stones in a ring read from directly above as nine flat shapes, each with a narrow strip of its front face showing under its lower edge — which is what the map-site skeleton now says — set evenly round a circle of short grass. That is MORE legible than the isometric reading, not less: from overhead the ring is a circle and the grazed interior is open inside it, where a three-quarter view foreshortens the circle into an ellipse and hides the far side of the grass behind the near stones. The grazed interior is this picture's one piece of evidence of the Vellsire, so it is the thing that must not be hidden. The old claim that the composition 'only works with height' is withdrawn. 'Tall' on these stones is now a content word rather than a picture dimension, which incidentally settles the tension classes['map-site']._gate recorded: there is no drawn height left to bound, so the ceiling can be stated on both drawn axes without inverting a silhouette. No roof or wall material applies here; the class carries no buildings clause and none is needed. || CENTRE — this is the one node where a prop sits exactly on the spawn tile: sanctum-antler-ring (antler-stone, x512 y512, signChain vellsire-chain) IS the ring. _player._source: build-doc §9.2 / locked decision L6 — 'verbatim in every player prompt … never `cape` or `cloak`'. The trial graph's embedded prompt DROPS the cap clause, so it is not canon; this string is.
_player.subject: young field warden protagonist wearing a green shirt, brown shorts, a peaked green ranger cap with a small yellow star badge, a leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and brown walking boots
_player.seedPinSource: gate B0. 42 is the validated trial seed (the handoff's 62 is the CLIPLoader node id) and it is the seed the APPROVED player sprite was generated with (tools/comfy/manifest-b0.json#player-front). G5: it is frozen for every player row.
_player._walkNote: EMPTY, AND THAT IS §9.6 STEP 4 TAKING ITS OWN FALLBACK. The walk trial's exit condition is 'Fail ⇒ fall to bob without discussion', and the bob is what shipped: build-doc §9.6 step 4, 'y = 2px sine per tile step, 1px lateral sway, horizontal flip alternation', implemented in game/movement.ts (skipOffsetPx / skipSwayOffsetPx / skipFlipped) off balance.map.skipHopPx, skipSwayPx and skipHopsPerTile. The third term is why there is no frame here: the horizontal mirror on alternate hops is what a step frame would have been for — a pure vertical sine on a static sprite reads as a float, and the mirror is what makes the eye read a change of weight. Six img2img rows for frames nothing can draw would be real money spent on unreachable art.

approvedFront.note: Lane B integration: this manifest's player-front row carries the approval, so a rebuild cannot silently re-render the protagonist.

_player._staticsNote: ONE, and it was three. Hank's ruling: "we're switching to the player character always being facing forward and doing the skipping movement as it moves around." The player never turns, so back and side are views the screen has no route to — game/mapview.ts PLAYER_VIEWS is ["front"] and playerArtIds() is one key, held to SET IDENTITY with this class by tests/gates/dex-path-contract.test.ts. See _deviations LB-M10.

_versionsNote: build-doc §8.4's licensed escape, persisted: 'any asset regenerated must reuse its manifest seed unless the manifest entry is versioned'. deriveRows() reads a row's version from here, so a bump survives `rebuild` and actually moves the seed. Bump either this map or the row's own `version` field and run `rebuild` — the rebuild promotes a row-level bump into this map, clears that row's recorded seed/file (the old art is superseded, not deleted) and sets it back to pending. An id absent from this map is version 1.

_img2img._source: At the handoff there was no img2img workflow: none existed, none could be retrieved, none had been trialled. The graph has since been BUILT and EXECUTED (the upload endpoint is verified and a denoise sweep ran off the approved player static), but that sweep established a LIMIT rather than an approval — img2img on this model is for deltas within a view and cannot turn one. Neither of the two uses build-doc asks for, §9.5 map year variants and §9.6 walk frames, has been run and reviewed.
_img2img._enforcement: While this is false, comfy-batch's assertSupervised() refuses any batch containing more than ONE img2img row, with or without --confirm. Set it to true only after one image has been generated through tools/comfy/img2img.ts and reviewed by a human.
